We have applied template 1914393 to target molecule. The result is a tuple of two SMILES: product fragments? Actually retrosynthesis: applying template yields precursors. The result shows a tuple of two SMILES: 'COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1' and 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'. Wait the first is similar to target but missing something? Let's compare target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. The result first SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1. That seems to be the core where the triazine? Actually target has a 1,2,4-triazine? The result shows a ring with nn[nH]c2N (maybe a 1,2,4-triazol?). The second SMILES: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That's a protected amine? It contains F and Cl substituents.

We need to produce a route with at least 3 reactions using templates 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395 in that order. So we need to apply 1914393 first to get two fragments. Then apply 1914394 to one of those fragments (presumably the one containing a CCl group) to break that CCl bond. Then apply 1914395 to the other fragment maybe to replace F with O? Actually template 1914395 is a retro transformation that replaces a fluorine attached to a carbon in a heterocycle with an OH (i.e., O-CH-... to F-CH-...). The retro direction: O-CH... -> F-CH... So forward direction is fluorination of a heterocycle. In retrosynthesis, we would replace a fluorine with OH. So we need a fragment that contains a fluorine attached to a carbon in a heterocycle. The second fragment from 1914393 is FC1CN(... )C1, which has a fluorine attached to carbon of a saturated ring (maybe a fluoromethyl). That matches template 1914395? The template expects [F]-[CH]1-[C]-[#7]-[C]-1 (a fluorinated azetidine?). The fragment is FC1CN(... )C1, which is a fluoromethyl attached to a 4-membered ring? Actually C1CN(Cc2... )C1 is a morpholine-like? It's a 5-membered? Let's parse: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That's a fluoromethyl attached to a 5-membered ring (maybe azetidine). The ring: C1 C N (substituent) C1. That's a 3-member? Actually C1 C N C1 is a 3-member? Not sure. But template may apply.

Thus step 2: apply template 1914394 to the second fragment to replace CCl with something else? Template 1914394 is a retro that breaks a CCl bond to give a CH2Cl and the aromatic ring? Let's examine template 1914394: retro_smarts: '[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[c;H0;D3;+0:8](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Cl;D1;H0:2]):[c:9]:[c:10]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Cl;D1;H0:2].[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[cH;D2;+0:8]:[c:9]:[c:10]:1'

So retro direction: starting from a molecule with a -CH2Cl attached to aromatic ring and a substituent (maybe a side chain) and a nitrogen attached to aromatic ring, it splits into a dichloromethyl (Cl-CH2-Cl) and the aromatic amide? Actually product side: Cl-CH2-Cl (dichloromethane) and the aromatic amine? The forward direction (synthetic) would be coupling of dichloromethane to aromatic? Not sure.

Our fragment has CCl attached to aromatic ring: Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2. That's a benzyl with CCl substituent (chloromethyl). The fragment also has a fluoromethyl attached to a heterocycle. The template expects a CH2Cl attached to aromatic ring and a nitrogen attached to aromatic ring (anilide). In our fragment, we have a nitrogen attached to the heterocycle, not aromatic. Wait the fragment: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. The aromatic ring is attached via a CH2 to the nitrogen of the heterocycle. The aromatic ring has a CCl substituent (chloromethyl). The template expects the aromatic ring attached to nitrogen directly? Actually pattern: [#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1... So nitrogen attached to carbon attached to aromatic ring. In our fragment, the nitrogen is attached to a carbon (the heterocycle carbon) which is attached to aromatic via CH2? Let's see: N(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2) means nitrogen attached to CH2 (C) which attaches to aromatic. So pattern maybe matches: N-CH2-aryl. The template expects N-C-aryl where the aryl carbon is part of aromatic ring (c). In our case, the carbon attached to N is aliphatic (CH2) not aromatic. So maybe not match.

Maybe we should apply template 1914394 to the first fragment? The first fragment: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1. This has an aniline (N attached to aromatic). It also has a CH2Cl? No. So not.

Thus maybe the order is: first 1914393 splits target into two fragments: fragment A (core) and fragment B (side chain). Then apply 1914394 to fragment B to break the CCl bond, generating a chloromethyl reagent and the heterocycle? Actually template 1914394 retro splits a molecule that has a CH2Cl attached to aromatic and a nitrogen attached to aromatic into two pieces: dichloromethane and the aromatic amine (without CH2Cl). So applying to fragment B (which contains CCl) would give two pieces: dichloromethane (Cl-CH2-Cl) and the heterocycle without the CCl substituent? Let's test by applying template 1914394 to fragment B.
